title: Entretien avec la direction  (Meeting with the Boss)

segments.t: In the executive office at ASK, agency owner Hicham discusses maternity arrangements with Andrea. While Hicham frames his questions as benevolent managerial concern, Andrea maintains strict professional boundaries. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Je sais que ce n'est pas facile.
On a chacun notre tempérament, c'est humain.
On avait dit que je gérais ma grossesse seule.
Je me soucie de la santé de mes employés.
Oui, je te remercie de ta bienveillance.
Je reste à ta disposition pour ton congé.
Je te demanderai quand je ressentirai le besoin.
C'est noté. Tout va bien avec ta compagne?
Très bien, merci.
J'en suis ravi. Transmets-lui mes amitiés.
Je n'y manquerai pas.
Bonne journée, Andréa.
Cordialement, Hicham.
Je viens voir Jean Dujardin maintenant.
Fais attention à toi sur la route.
Ne t'inquiète pas, je gère tout.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Je sais que ce n'est pas facile.
'I know that it is not easy.' Hicham acknowledges the workplace pressure. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'know'.
On a chacun notre tempérament, c'est humain.
'We each have our temperament, it is human.' Hicham makes an empathetic concession. Notice how the short vowel drops before a vowel sound around 'have', making the phrase flow smoothly as one unit.
On avait dit que je gérais ma grossesse seule.
'We agreed that I would manage my pregnancy alone.' Andrea sets firm boundaries. The adjective meaning 'alone' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
Je me soucie de la santé de mes employés.
'I care about the health of my employees.' Hicham defends his managerial intervention. Notice how 'care' leads directly into the noun meaning 'health'.
Oui, je te remercie de ta bienveillance.
'Yes, I thank you for your benevolence.' Andrea responds with polite formality. The informal 'you' form around 'thank' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Je reste à ta disposition pour ton congé.
'I remain at your disposal for your leave.' Hicham offers administrative support. The verb meaning 'remain' pairs naturally with the noun for 'leave' in everyday conversation.
Je te demanderai quand je ressentirai le besoin.
'I will ask you when I feel the need.' Andrea defers taking maternity leave. Andrea uses the casual singular 'you' with 'will ask', showing close familiarity.
C'est noté. Tout va bien avec ta compagne?
'It is noted. Is everything going well with your partner?' Hicham inquires courteously about family life. The informal 'you' form around 'it is' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Très bien, merci.
'Very well, thank you.' Andrea keeps her personal life concise. The key noun here means 'thank you', anchored by its matching French article.
J'en suis ravi. Transmets-lui mes amitiés.
'I am delighted. Pass along my warm regards to her.' Hicham closes the personal inquiry warmly. Notice how 'pass along to her' leads directly into the noun meaning 'regards'.
Je n'y manquerai pas.
'I will not fail to do so.' Andrea confirms with standard polite phrasing. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'will fail'.
Bonne journée, Andréa.
'Have a good day, Andrea.' Hicham brings the formal discussion to an end. The adjective meaning 'good' takes its feminine form here to match the noun it describes.
Cordialement, Hicham.
'Cordially, Hicham.' Andrea delivers a delightfully brisk, email-style farewell. The adverb meaning 'cordially' gives the reply its conversational emphasis.
Je viens voir Jean Dujardin maintenant.
'I am going to see Jean Dujardin now.' Andrea announces her immediate off-site priority. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'come'.
Fais attention à toi sur la route.
'Take care of yourself on the road.' Hicham reiterates his paternalistic care. The informal 'you' form around 'take care' marks a direct, personal relationship.
Ne t'inquiète pas, je gère tout.

'Do not worry, I manage everything.' Andrea reasserts total command of her affairs. The clause hinges on the everyday verb meaning 'worry'. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.

In his office, Hicham checks in on Andrea's pregnancy and offers maternity assistance. When you watch the episode, listen out for the expressions meaning 'know' and 'easy'. You'll catch them now. See you next time!
À bientôt!
